results.question: How long after signing can a draft rookie be traded?
results.answer: A Draft Rookie who signs a Standard NBA Contract cannot be traded before thirty (30) days following the date on which the contract is signed [Article VII, Section 8(d)].

results.question: How often can a team use the Bi-annual Exception?
results.answer: A team may not use all or any portion of the Bi-annual Exception in any two (2) consecutive Salary Cap Years [Article VII, Section 6(d)(3)].

results.question: How long can a Bi-annual Exception contract be?
results.answer: A Player Contract signed pursuant to the Bi-annual Exception cannot exceed two (2) Seasons in length [Article VII, Section 6(d)(2)]. Additionally, the remaining term of a contract acquired by assignment pursuant to the Bi-annual Exception may not exceed two (2) Seasons in length [Article VII, Section 6(d)(2)].

results.question: How long can a Non-Taxpayer Mid-Level contract be?
results.answer: A Player Contract signed or acquired by assignment using the Non-Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception cannot exceed four (4) Seasons in length [Article VII, Section 6(e)(2)].

results.question: Can a team above the second apron aggregate player salaries in a trade?
results.answer: No. A trade acquiring a player using the Aggregated Standard Traded Player Exception is prohibited if, immediately following the trade, the team's Apron Team Salary would exceed the Second Apron Level ($189.5 million) [Article VII, Section 2(e)(5)].
